front: Two point charges \( Q_1 = 2\ \mu\text{C} \) and \( Q_2 = 3\ \mu\text{C} \) are separated by \( 30\ \text{cm} \) in free space. Find the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them.
explanation: Use Coulomb's law \( F = \dfrac{k Q_1 Q_2}{r^{2}} \) with \( k \approx 8.99\times10^{9}\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2} \). Substitute \( r = 0.30\ \text{m} \): \( F = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^{9})(2\times10^{-6})(3\times10^{-6})}{(0.30)^{2}} \). The numerator is \( 5.39\times10^{-2} \) and \( (0.30)^{2} = 0.09 \), so \( F \approx 0.60\ \text{N} \).

front: Find the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of \( 2\ \text{m} \) from a \( +10\ \text{nC} \) point charge in free space.
explanation: The field of a point charge is \( E = \dfrac{kQ}{r^{2}} \) with \( k \approx 8.99\times10^{9}\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2} \). Substitute \( Q = 10\times10^{-9}\ \text{C} \) and \( r = 2\ \text{m} \): \( E = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^{9})(10\times10^{-9})}{2^{2}} = \dfrac{89.9}{4} \). Therefore \( E \approx 22.5\ \text{V/m} \), directed radially outward.

front: A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area \( 0.02\ \text{m}^{2} \) and plate separation \( 1\ \text{mm} \), filled with a dielectric of relative permittivity \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \). Find its capacitance.
explanation: Parallel-plate capacitance is \( C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r A}{d} \) with \( \varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}\ \text{F/m} \). Substitute \( A = 0.02\ \text{m}^{2} \), \( d = 1\times10^{-3}\ \text{m} \), and \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \): \( C = \dfrac{(8.854\times10^{-12})(4)(0.02)}{1\times10^{-3}} \). This gives \( C \approx 7.08\times10^{-10}\ \text{F} = 708\ \text{pF} \).

front: A \( 10\ \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is charged to \( 50\ \text{V} \). Find the energy stored in the capacitor.
explanation: The energy stored in a capacitor is \( W = \tfrac{1}{2} C V^{2} \). Substitute \( C = 10\times10^{-6}\ \text{F} \) and \( V = 50\ \text{V} \): \( W = \tfrac{1}{2}(10\times10^{-6})(50)^{2} \). Since \( (50)^{2} = 2500 \), \( W = \tfrac{1}{2}(10\times10^{-6})(2500) = 1.25\times10^{-2}\ \text{J} = 12.5\ \text{mJ} \).

front: A long straight wire in air carries a current of \( 10\ \text{A} \). Find the magnetic flux density at a radial distance of \( 5\ \text{cm} \) from the wire.
explanation: For a long straight wire, Ampere's law gives \( B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \) with \( \mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{H/m} \). Substitute \( I = 10\ \text{A} \) and \( r = 0.05\ \text{m} \): \( B = \dfrac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})(10)}{2\pi(0.05)} \). This simplifies to \( B = \dfrac{(2\times10^{-7})(10)}{0.05} = 4\times10^{-5}\ \text{T} = 40\ \mu\text{T} \).

front: A straight conductor of length \( 0.5\ \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 4\ \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.8\ \text{T} \). Find the magnitude of the force on the conductor.
explanation: The force on a current-carrying conductor is \( F = B I L \sin\theta \). The current is perpendicular to the field, so \( \theta = 90^{\circ} \) and \( \sin\theta = 1 \). Substitute the values: \( F = (0.8)(4)(0.5)(1) = 1.6\ \text{N} \).

front: The magnetic flux through a \( 100 \)-turn coil changes uniformly from \( 2\ \text{mWb} \) to \( 10\ \text{mWb} \) in \( 4\ \text{ms} \). Find the magnitude of the induced EMF.
explanation: Faraday's law gives \( |\mathcal{E}| = N\left|\dfrac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}\right| \). Here \( \Delta\Phi = 10 - 2 = 8\ \text{mWb} = 8\times10^{-3}\ \text{Wb} \) and \( \Delta t = 4\times10^{-3}\ \text{s} \). Thus \( |\mathcal{E}| = 100 \times \dfrac{8\times10^{-3}}{4\times10^{-3}} = 100 \times 2 = 200\ \text{V} \).

front: A lossless transmission line has a distributed inductance of \( 250\ \text{nH/m} \) and a distributed capacitance of \( 100\ \text{pF/m} \). Find the characteristic impedance of the line.
explanation: For a lossless line, \( Z_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{C}} \). Substitute \( L = 250\times10^{-9}\ \text{H/m} \) and \( C = 100\times10^{-12}\ \text{F/m} \): \( \dfrac{L}{C} = \dfrac{250\times10^{-9}}{100\times10^{-12}} = 2500 \). Therefore \( Z_0 = \sqrt{2500} = 50\ \Omega \).

front: A \( 50\ \Omega \) transmission line is terminated with a \( 75\ \Omega \) resistive load. Find the voltage reflection coefficient at the load.
explanation: The reflection coefficient is \( \Gamma = \dfrac{Z_L - Z_0}{Z_L + Z_0} \). Substitute \( Z_L = 75\ \Omega \) and \( Z_0 = 50\ \Omega \): \( \Gamma = \dfrac{75 - 50}{75 + 50} = \dfrac{25}{125} \). Therefore \( \Gamma = 0.2 \) (real and positive).

front: The magnitude of the voltage reflection coefficient on a transmission line is \( 0.5 \). Find the standing-wave ratio (SWR).
explanation: The standing-wave ratio is \( \text{SWR} = \dfrac{1 + |\Gamma|}{1 - |\Gamma|} \). Substitute \( |\Gamma| = 0.5 \): \( \text{SWR} = \dfrac{1 + 0.5}{1 - 0.5} = \dfrac{1.5}{0.5} \). Therefore \( \text{SWR} = 3 \).

front: An electromagnetic wave propagates in free space at a frequency of \( 3\ \text{GHz} \). Find its wavelength. (Use \( c = 3\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s} \).)
explanation: Wavelength and frequency are related by \( \lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} \). Substitute \( c = 3\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s} \) and \( f = 3\times10^{9}\ \text{Hz} \): \( \lambda = \dfrac{3\times10^{8}}{3\times10^{9}} \). Therefore \( \lambda = 0.1\ \text{m} = 10\ \text{cm} \).

front: A uniform plane wave propagates in a lossless, nonmagnetic dielectric with relative permittivity \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \). Find the phase velocity of the wave. (Use \( c = 3\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s} \).)
explanation: In a nonmagnetic medium (\( \mu_r = 1 \)), the phase velocity is \( v_p = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}} \). Substitute \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \): \( v_p = \dfrac{3\times10^{8}}{\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{3\times10^{8}}{2} \). Therefore \( v_p = 1.5\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s} \).

front: Find the intrinsic (wave) impedance of a lossless, nonmagnetic medium with relative permittivity \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \). Use the free-space intrinsic impedance \( \eta_0 \approx 377\ \Omega \).
explanation: For a nonmagnetic medium, \( \eta = \dfrac{\eta_0}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}} \). Substitute \( \eta_0 = 377\ \Omega \) and \( \varepsilon_r = 4 \): \( \eta = \dfrac{377}{\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{377}{2} \). Therefore \( \eta \approx 188.5\ \Omega \).

front: A long air-core solenoid has \( 500 \) turns wound uniformly over a length of \( 25\ \text{cm} \) and carries \( 2\ \text{A} \). Find the magnetic flux density near the center of the solenoid.
explanation: Inside a long solenoid, \( B = \mu_0 n I \), where \( n = N/\ell \) is the number of turns per unit length. Here \( n = \dfrac{500}{0.25} = 2000\ \text{turns/m} \). Then \( B = (4\pi\times10^{-7})(2000)(2) \approx 5.03\times10^{-3}\ \text{T} = 5.03\ \text{mT} \).

front: An infinite line charge in free space has a uniform linear charge density of \( 5\ \text{nC/m} \). Find the magnitude of the electric field at a radial distance of \( 10\ \text{cm} \).
explanation: For an infinite line charge, \( E = \dfrac{\rho_\ell}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r} = \dfrac{2k\rho_\ell}{r} \) with \( k \approx 8.99\times10^{9} \). Substitute \( \rho_\ell = 5\times10^{-9}\ \text{C/m} \) and \( r = 0.10\ \text{m} \): \( E = \dfrac{2(8.99\times10^{9})(5\times10^{-9})}{0.10} \). Therefore \( E \approx 899\ \text{V/m} \).

front: A uniform plane wave in free space has a frequency of \( 150\ \text{MHz} \). Find its phase constant \( \beta \). (Use \( c = 3\times10^{8}\ \text{m/s} \).)
explanation: The phase constant is \( \beta = \dfrac{\omega}{c} = \dfrac{2\pi f}{c} \). Substitute \( f = 150\times10^{6}\ \text{Hz} \): \( \beta = \dfrac{2\pi(150\times10^{6})}{3\times10^{8}} = 2\pi(0.5) \). Therefore \( \beta = \pi \approx 3.14\ \text{rad/m} \).
